relations.formulaHTML: a verb used with de + de + someone, something or an action
relations.rule: Some verbs use de to link to what follows. Learn the verb and de together.

examples.targetHTML: Me acuerdo de ti.
examples.translation: I remember you.

examples.targetHTML: No se acuerda de ella.
examples.translation: He doesn’t remember her.

examples.targetHTML: Se trata de un asunto importante.
examples.translation: It's about an important matter.

examples.targetHTML: Eso depende de muchos factores.
examples.translation: That depends on many factors.

examples.targetHTML: No te olvides de cerrar la puerta.
examples.translation: Don't forget to close the door.

relations.formulaHTML: a thing or time + de + a detail or an action
relations.rule: Adds a detail about ownership, contents, material or purpose, including an action: hora de comer = time to eat.
relations.translation: I want a glass of water.

examples.targetHTML: Quiero un vaso de agua.
examples.translation: I want a glass of water.

examples.targetHTML: Una hermosa mesa de madera.
examples.translation: A beautiful wooden table.

examples.targetHTML: Es hora de comer.
examples.translation: It is time to eat.

examples.targetHTML: Un amigo de mi hermano nos visitó.
examples.translation: A friend of my brother visited us.

examples.targetHTML: Un día de descanso muy merecido.
examples.translation: A well-deserved day of rest.

relations.formulaHTML: think, say, know or hope + que + what happens
relations.rule: Links what someone thinks, says, knows or hopes to a statement.
relations.translation: I think it’s going to rain.

examples.targetHTML: Creo que va a llover.
examples.translation: I think it’s going to rain.

examples.targetHTML: Ella dijo que vendría temprano.
examples.translation: She said she would come early.

examples.targetHTML: Sé que tienes toda la razón.
examples.translation: I know you are completely right.

examples.targetHTML: Espero que todo salga bien.
examples.translation: I hope everything turns out well.

examples.targetHTML: Él pensaba que era el momento oportuno.
examples.translation: He thought it was the right moment.

relations.formulaHTML: someone or something + que + more about them or it
relations.rule: Adds information about the person or thing just mentioned.
relations.targetHTML: Es el libro que estoy leyendo.
relations.translation: It is the book that I am reading.

examples.targetHTML: Es el libro que estoy leyendo.
examples.translation: It is the book that I am reading.

examples.targetHTML: La persona que llamó no dejó mensaje.
examples.translation: The person who called left no message.

examples.targetHTML: La película que vimos fue excelente.
examples.translation: The movie we saw was excellent.

examples.targetHTML: El lugar que conocimos era precioso.
examples.translation: The place we visited was lovely.

examples.targetHTML: Son cosas que pasan todos los días.
examples.translation: These are things that happen every day.

relations.formulaHTML: more, less or better + que + what you compare with
relations.rule: Means “than” when comparing people, things or situations.
relations.targetHTML: Ella es más alta que yo.

examples.targetHTML: Ella es más alta que yo.
examples.translation: She is taller than me.

examples.targetHTML: Esto es mejor que lo que teníamos.
examples.translation: This is better than what we had.

examples.targetHTML: Tardamos menos tiempo que ayer.
examples.translation: We took less time than yesterday.

examples.targetHTML: La casa es más grande que el piso anterior.
examples.translation: The house is bigger than the previous flat.

examples.targetHTML: Hoy hace más calor que la semana pasada.
examples.translation: Today is hotter than last week.

relations.rule: Can mean “oneself”, or belong with a verb such as sentirse (feel). It does not always mean “oneself”.

examples.targetHTML: Él se lava la cara.
examples.translation: He washes his face.

examples.targetHTML: Ella se miró en el espejo.
examples.translation: She looked at herself in the mirror.

examples.targetHTML: Se siente mucho más tranquilo ahora.
examples.translation: He feels much calmer now.

examples.targetHTML: Los niños se levantaron temprano.
examples.translation: The children got up early.

examples.targetHTML: El actor se vistió con elegancia.
examples.translation: The actor dressed elegantly.

relations.rule: Describes what happens without naming who does it. Compare se habla (people speak) and se venden libros (books are sold).

examples.targetHTML: Aquí se habla español.
examples.translation: Spanish is spoken here.

examples.targetHTML: Se venden libros antiguos.
examples.translation: Old books are for sale.

examples.targetHTML: Se come muy bien en este restaurante.
examples.translation: The food is very good at this restaurant.

examples.targetHTML: Se vive con tranquilidad en este pueblo.
examples.translation: Life is peaceful in this village.

examples.targetHTML: Se espera una gran multitud hoy.
examples.translation: A large crowd is expected today.

relations.rule: With a describing word, means “the … thing” or “the … part”: lo importante = the important thing.
relations.translation: The important thing is to participate.

examples.targetHTML: Lo importante es participar.
examples.translation: The important thing is to participate.

examples.targetHTML: Lo bueno es que tenemos tiempo de sobra.
examples.translation: The good thing is that we have plenty of time.

examples.targetHTML: Lo difícil ya ha pasado.
examples.translation: The difficult part has already passed.

examples.targetHTML: Hizo lo mejor que pudo.
examples.translation: He did the best he could.

examples.targetHTML: Lo curioso es que nadie notó la diferencia.
examples.translation: The curious thing is that nobody noticed the difference.

relations.rule: Refers to “him”, a masculine “it”, or an idea: lo sé = I know that.

examples.targetHTML: Ya lo sé.
examples.translation: I already know that.

examples.targetHTML: No lo entiendo con claridad.
examples.translation: I do not understand it clearly.

examples.targetHTML: ¿Lo has visto por aquí?
examples.translation: Have you seen him around here?

examples.targetHTML: Lo hice exactamente como me pediste.
examples.translation: I did it exactly as you asked me.

examples.targetHTML: Si tienes el informe, lo leo esta noche.
examples.translation: If you have the report, I'll read it tonight.

relations.rule: Refers to us: someone sees or helps us, or tells us something.

examples.targetHTML: El profesor nos enseña bien.
examples.translation: The teacher teaches us well.

examples.targetHTML: Ellos nos invitaron a cenar.
examples.translation: They invited us for dinner.

examples.targetHTML: El guía nos mostró la ciudad vieja.
examples.translation: The guide showed us the old city.

examples.targetHTML: Un vecino nos ayudó con el coche.
examples.translation: A neighbour helped us with the car.

examples.targetHTML: Ella nos espera aquí.
examples.translation: She is waiting for us here.

relations.rule: Here, a + el becomes al: “to the” or “at the”.
relations.translation: We are going to the cinema tonight.

examples.targetHTML: Vamos al cine esta noche.
examples.translation: We are going to the cinema tonight.

examples.targetHTML: Llegamos al parque al atardecer.
examples.translation: We arrived at the park at sunset.

examples.targetHTML: Tuve que ir al médico por la mañana.
examples.translation: I had to go to the doctor in the morning.

examples.targetHTML: Acompañó a su abuelo al aeropuerto.
examples.translation: He accompanied his grandfather to the airport.

examples.targetHTML: Volvieron al trabajo con energía.
examples.translation: They returned to work with energy.

relations.formulaHTML: al + a verb in its dictionary form
relations.rule: Means “when” doing something: al llegar = when someone arrives.
relations.translation: When I got home, I rested.

examples.targetHTML: Al llegar a casa, descansé.
examples.translation: When I got home, I rested.

examples.targetHTML: Al oír la campana, salieron todos.
examples.translation: When everyone heard the bell, they left.

examples.targetHTML: Sonrió al ver el regalo.
examples.translation: She smiled when she saw the gift.

examples.targetHTML: Al abrir la ventana entró aire fresco.
examples.translation: When the window was opened, fresh air came in.

examples.targetHTML: Al terminar el discurso, todos aplaudieron.
examples.translation: When the speech ended, everyone applauded.
